transitions.historical_text: Discard 1 card from your hand. During this turn, any damage you take from your opponent becomes 0.
transitions.modern_text: Discard 1 card from your hand. This turn, any damage you take from your opponent's cards and effects becomes 0.
transitions.summary: Wording only: 'During this turn, any damage you take from your opponent becomes 0' becomes 'This turn, any damage you take from your opponent's cards and effects becomes 0'. Same resolution - all damage from the opponent is reduced to 0 for the turn, with the discard still a cost.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (SGX1-ENE18, Speed Duel GX: Duel Academy Box)

transitions.historical_text: Discard 1 card from your hand. This turn, any damage you take from your opponent's cards and effects becomes 0.
transitions.modern_text: Discard 1 card; you take no damage from your opponent's cards this turn, also your monsters cannot be destroyed by battle this turn.
transitions.summary: Functional erratum: the card gained a second clause making your monsters immune to battle destruction for the turn. The GOAT script registers only the damage-to-zero field effect; the modern script additionally registers a field EFFECT_INDESTRUCTABLE_BATTLE with EFFECT_FLAG_IGNORE_IMMUNE over your Monster Zone, resetting at the End Phase. Before the erratum the card stops damage and nothing else.

rulings_check.difference: Era: the card only stops damage; your monsters can still be destroyed by battle. Modern: your monsters also cannot be destroyed by battle this turn.

review.notes:
Upstream annotates the goat variant 'Doesn't prevent battle destruction', which matches the script diff exactly - the only removed lines are the EFFECT_INDESTRUCTABLE_BATTLE block. Remaining diff lines are bitwise-or vs addition of disjoint flags and are equivalent. Both GOAT (2005-04-01) and Edison (2010-04-24) fall well before the 2022 erratum, so both take the baseline implementation.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Hallowed Life Barrier). The rulings read support d1 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. Verdicts: [c1] d1 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu.
